outcome: The full question (does a nontrivial elementary embedding j:V→V exist consistently with ZF alone) remains open, but a major necessary sub-case moved: Farmer Schlutzenberg proved (arXiv:2006.01077, decisive version v4 posted 2024-03-18, published in Journal of Mathematical Logic 25(2), 2025) that ZF plus the existence of a Kunen-type embedding j:V_{λ+2}→V_{λ+2} (for λ even) is consistent relative to ZFC + I0, contrary to the natural expectation (from the ZFC Kunen inconsistency) that ZF alone might already refute it. Since any Reinhardt embedding j:V→V restricts to give such a V_{λ+2}→V_{λ+2} embedding, this removes what many set theorists expected to be an easy obstruction and is widely treated as the most significant recent movement on this question, earning Schlutzenberg the 2026 Hausdorff Medal of the European Set Theory Society.

disputes.summary: Rupert McCallum posted an arXiv preprint (2601.10231, v1 2026-01-15) claiming the next level up, inconsistency of a nontrivial Σ1-elementary embedding j:V_{λ+3}≺V_{λ+3} with ZF — a stronger and more directly relevant claim toward refuting the full V→V question. The author withdrew it (v3, 2026-08-23) after finding an error in the 'continuity of Skolem functions' argument in the final section. This is a withdrawn claim, not a settled result, and is recorded here as an instructive incident rather than as the record's main event; McCallum made and withdrew a similar claim in 2017-2018 as well (predates the window, not counted).

summary: The frozen Wikipedia bullet asks whether ZF alone (without choice) can consistently admit a nontrivial elementary embedding j:V→V. This remains fully open as stated: no proof of consistency or inconsistency of the full V→V embedding with ZF alone has been published or claimed since 26 January 2024. However, a closely related necessary sub-case did move. Any Reinhardt embedding j:V→V restricts to an embedding j↾V_{λ+2}:V_{λ+2}→V_{λ+2} for λ = sup_n j^n(κ), so the existence of such a 'Kunen cardinal' embedding is a necessary consequence of (and hence a genuine case of) the full question. Farmer Schlutzenberg's paper (arXiv:2006.01077, originally posted 2020 but decisively revised as v4 on 2024-03-18, inside the research window, and published in the Journal of Mathematical Logic in 2025) proved that ZF + 'there is an elementary embedding j:V_{λ+2}→V_{λ+2}' is consistent relative to ZFC + I0 (for λ even) — i.e. this weaker embedding is NOT refutable from ZF alone the way Kunen refuted it from ZFC, a genuinely surprising result that won the 2026 Hausdorff Medal. This is a `partial` result in the sense of §3.1: it settles (positively, modulo relative consistency) a necessary case of the stated question, without resolving the full V→V question itself, so status is `partial` and resolution_direction is `confirmed` (the natural conjecture that ZF alone might refute even this weaker embedding was refuted; the embedding's consistency was confirmed relative to I0). Separately, in January 2026 Rupert McCallum posted a preprint (arXiv:2601.10231) claiming to prove inconsistency of ZF with a nontrivial Σ1-elementary j:V_{λ+3}≺V_{λ+3}, one level stronger and directly bearing on the general question; he withdrew it in August 2026 after finding a flaw, and it is recorded as an unresolved incident in `disputes` rather than as the primary event, since a withdrawn claim carries no result. No AI system is mentioned anywhere in the Schlutzenberg paper, the McCallum preprint, or the other 2024-2025 papers I examined (Mohammd 2025 on eventually dominating functions, Jeon 2024 on cofinal Reinhardt embeddings without Powerset) — this is standard, entirely human, pen-and-paper large cardinal set theory with no LLM, theorem-prover, or automated-search component disclosed by any author. The triage's verdict of `none` for AI involvement is correct, but I disagree with treating the problem as having seen no relevant movement: the Schlutzenberg result, though dated by preprint history to 2020-2024 with a 2024 decisive revision, is squarely inside the window by its operative posting date and is a substantial, high-profile case of this exact bullet.
competing_reading: One could argue Schlutzenberg's result is really about a different, weaker statement ('Kunen cardinal' / V_{λ+2} embeddings) rather than a case of 'the' Reinhardt/V→V question, since the Wikipedia bullet's literal object j:V→V is a proper-class embedding of the whole universe, and no first-order formalization of that exists without moving to NBG/KM (a point the Reinhardt cardinal article itself makes). Under a strict reading, V_{λ+2}→V_{λ+2} is a related-but-distinct, weaker large cardinal notion, and settling it would be a related problem, not a case, making the correct status `open` rather than `partial`. I judge `partial` to be the better reading because the restriction relationship is not merely analogical: existence of a full Reinhardt embedding provably implies existence of a Kunen-cardinal embedding (this is the actual mathematical content of Kunen's own inconsistency argument), so 'is ZF-with-Kunen-cardinal consistent' is a logically necessary condition for 'is ZF-with-Reinhardt-cardinal consistent', which is exactly what makes it a restriction/case in the sense of §3.1 rather than a change of the question. Also worth flagging: I could not fully extract the Schlutzenberg PDF text (encoding issues) and relied on WebFetch's markdown-converted renderings plus the Hausdorff Medal citation for corroboration, so there is a small residual chance of an inaccuracy carried over from the fetch tool's summarization rather than my own reading of primary text.
what_would_settle_it: A published proof (peer-reviewed, or at least surviving expert scrutiny for a couple of years) either constructing a nontrivial j:V→V (in some workable class-theoretic sense, e.g. NBG/KM) consistent with ZF, or refuting it, would resolve the bullet outright. Short of that, a non-withdrawn version of a V_{λ+3}-level or higher inconsistency result (of the kind McCallum attempted) would be the next incremental case to watch, since the chain of decreasing embedding strengths (V_{λ+2}, V_{λ+3}, ..., V→V) forms a natural ladder toward the full question.

judgement.doubts: Schlutzenberg's result is first posted in 2020 (arXiv 2006.01077, same title); the record gives no evidence that v4 (2024-03-18) contains new mathematics, only calling it 'decisive'. Even if v4 were counted, consistency of a V_{λ+2} embedding is a necessary condition for, not a restriction of, the V→V question: it settles a weaker statement and does not decide the bullet in any sub-case, so it is a variant. Journal publication and the 2026 Hausdorff Medal make it digested, but that does not change scope.
